newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold volume back to normal as prices rise.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold volume back to normal as prices rise.

text.p: Istanbul gold exchange volume slipped to more normal levels on Monday, with 415 kg of trade from Friday's 2,111, as rising world gold prices prevented the arbitrage deals which had buoyed trade last week, dealers said.
Gold closed up slightly at $354.00 an ounce after $353.50 on Friday, following upward trends on world markets.
Gold also rose in lira terms to 1,313,800 lira per gram compared to Friday's 1,311,400 with the help of a weak lira which ended at 115,350 per dollar versus the previous 114,825.
"Trading was quieter due to the inability of banks to conduct arbitrage deals and the lack of physical demand in the free market," one dealer said.
Istanbul gold exchange trade was unusually active last week as falling gold prices enabled banks to arbitrage by buying gold in dollars and selling in lira.
Of the day's 415 kg of trade, 375 kg was conducted in the afternoon session. 53.0 percent of the total was traded in lira terms.
